principles: Keep milestone ledger, acceptance bindings, verificationIntent, and evidence as the only canonical owners of their existing facts.
Make topology reference-only and the matrix a deterministic L0 projection.
Preserve backward compatibility and lifecycle behavior in observe-only Wave 1.
Fail diagnostics deterministically on malformed, duplicate, unresolved, or self-authored topology references.
drivers: Reviewer must see the complete producer-to-consumer proof design before REVIEW without creating a second truth source.
Verification-intent ownership and PLAN freeze already provide the correct write boundary for planned paths.
A concrete, scriptable CLI transcript is required for user-visible acceptance and compatibility testing.

options.name: A: Nested topology plus dedicated acceptance_matrix command
pros: Matches the approved ownership model and keeps atomic ProofStory versioning.
Creates a clear read-only surface with deterministic JSON/text output.
Separates diagnostics from existing gate status so Wave 1 cannot accidentally change lifecycle semantics.

options.name: B: Nested topology rendered only through existing proofstory status
cons: Couples experimental topology output to existing gate diagnostics.
Makes read-only user acceptance and non-gating boundaries less isolated and harder to test.

options.name: C: Separate topology table or writable matrix artifact
pros: Could centralize rows in one new file.
cons: Creates a second writable truth source.
Violates the approved Wave 1 stop condition and risks drift from milestone/checklist/evidence owners.

chosen: A: Nested topology plus dedicated acceptance_matrix command
rationale: Choose A because it implements the approved nested ownership, gives users a precise deterministic read-only transcript, and isolates observe-only diagnostics from existing ProofStory lifecycle gates. The command derives rows at read time and persists nothing.

preMortem.scenario: Topology becomes a second author of producer-consumer semantics.
preMortem.trigger: Schema accepts inline endpoint prose or copied claims instead of stable refs.
preMortem.consequence: Matrix can appear complete while disagreeing with verificationIntent.
preMortem.mitigation: Normalize only typed reference objects and add a mutation test that inline/self-authored edge fields are rejected.

preMortem.scenario: Read-only renderer mutates runtime or story state.
preMortem.trigger: Command is omitted from read-only policy or handler writes cache/activity/evidence.
preMortem.consequence: A diagnostic changes auditable state and can masquerade as evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Register ownershipClass readOnly, add READ_ONLY_COMMANDS membership, and byte/hash-compare story/runtime artifacts before and after CLI execution.

preMortem.trigger: New diagnostics are consumed by phase gates or existing proofstory report status.
preMortem.consequence: Legacy and topology-missing Stories cannot progress despite observe rollout.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep evaluator separate from gate consumers and prove identical transition results for topology-enabled and legacy fixtures.

preMortem.scenario: Unstable ordering causes nondeterministic evidence and reviewer churn.
preMortem.trigger: Rows or diagnostics follow input/object iteration order.
preMortem.consequence: Equivalent inputs produce different transcripts and hashes.
preMortem.mitigation: Canonicalize stable IDs and sort bindings, refs, rows, and diagnostics; run permutation equality tests.

preMortem.trigger: Placeholder coverageBasisRef is treated as verified or discovery is inferred from caller topology.
preMortem.consequence: Reviewer trusts self-reported scope coverage before Wave 1A exists.
preMortem.mitigation: Render basis as unavailable/observe-only, use no complete verdict, and test that caller-authored completeness cannot be promoted.
